judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the first 'Thomann News' teaser card. It links to youtube.com/watch?v=7aDSIaFjkXM, and its name is 'YouTube Marie Leloup plays Golden from "Kpop Demon Hunters" in the new Thomann Shop!'. The third card has the same name apart from the casing of 'KPop' and links to Bx3MLITMdtM. Both cards are still on the live page. I checked both videos: each is on Thomann's own channel, has exactly that title and the same description. 7aDSIaFjkXM is a 31-second Short, and Bx3MLITMdtM is the 3:15 full video of the same performance. So the link text is the exact title of the video it opens and correctly describes where the link goes. The Understanding document for 2.4.4 says the name of the destination is enough to describe the link's purpose. It lists different text for links with different destinations only as a best practice. Both links deliver the content they advertise: Marie Leloup playing Golden in the Thomann shop, on YouTube. The ACT definition of 'equivalent resource' allows the destinations to contain different amounts of information. The finding treats 'different URL' as 'different purpose' and applies the best practice as a requirement, which is closer to 2.4.9 (AAA). This is a borderline call. The thumbnails differ visually (a vertical clip with blurred sides versus a 'VIOLIN COVER' title card), they are presentational (alt=""), and the proposed ACT rule fd3a94 could be read as failing an excerpt-versus-full pair. Even so, sighted users get no more information than screen-reader users about which card is the Short and which is the full video. Rampa never read the destinations.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the third 'Thomann News' teaser card. It links to youtube.com/watch?v=Bx3MLITMdtM, and its name is 'YouTube Marie Leloup plays Golden from "KPop Demon Hunters" in the new Thomann Shop!'. It is the pair of the first card (7aDSIaFjkXM), and both cards are still on the live page. According to YouTube's own data, both videos are on Thomann's channel and have the same title and description. This one is the full 3:15 video, and the other is a 31-second Short of the same performance. The link text is the destination's exact title and accurately describes what the link opens. Under 2.4.4 that is enough to determine the link's purpose. The Understanding document lists different text for different destinations as a best practice, not a requirement. Both destinations deliver the key content the link advertises, and ACT's 'equivalent resource' definition allows different amounts of information. The finding applies 'identical text must not lead to different URLs', which is stricter than 2.4.4 and is a best practice or 2.4.9 concern. The call is borderline. The thumbnails differ, they are presentational (alt=""), and the proposed ACT rule fd3a94 could be read as a fail for excerpt-versus-full versions. Still, neither the page nor the thumbnails tell sighted users which version is which, so screen-reader users lose little by comparison.
